prompt: A new helper in `brave/components/foo/` needs to know whether the user is signed in, and the quickest way is to `#include "brave/browser/..."`. Which statement about Chromium's layering explains the reviewer's objection?
choices: It's fine as long as the include is guarded by a buildflag that's off on iOS builds
Dependencies flow downward only; components can't depend on embedder code
Components may depend on any layer except `//base`
Only `//content` is off-limits to components; browser-layer includes are allowed
explain: Chromium layers (`//base` → core libs → `//content` → `//components` → embedders) allow dependencies **downward only**. `brave/browser/` is the embedder layer, so components can never reach up into it.

choices: Inject the URL loader factory via `Init()` params instead
Wrap the call in `#if !BUILDFLAG(IS_IOS)` so it compiles on every platform
Cache `g_browser_process` in a member to avoid repeated global lookups
Move the `g_browser_process` call into a lambda so it runs lazily on first use
explain: `components/` code must never use `g_browser_process` or depend on `brave/browser/` — that's a layering violation. Pass dependencies in via injection (constructor params, `Init()`, callbacks).

prompt: A component class currently takes a `Profile*` just to read a couple of prefs. Which signature follows the components layering rules?
choices: `void Init(Profile* profile);` plus an include of `chrome/browser/profiles/profile.h`
`void Init();` calling `ProfileManager::GetLastUsedProfile()` inside
`void Init(Browser* browser);` so it can reach the profile and window
`void Init(PrefService* prefs);`
explain: Never use `Profile` in components — pass `PrefService` (via `user_prefs::UserPrefs::Get(browser_context)`) or `BrowserContext` instead, and never include `chrome/browser/` or `brave/browser/` from `components/`.

choices: Fine as-is — `Profile*` is the standard handle for looking up services
Store a `Browser*` instead so other services are reachable later
Inject `ExtensionSystem*` directly; the class only needs that service
Replace `profile_` with a `raw_ref<Profile>` for memory safety
explain: Pass the most specific dependency, not a "bag of stuff" object. If `Profile` is only a lookup handle for one service, inject that service instead.

prompt:
A teammate wraps every caller like this:

```cpp
#if BUILDFLAG(BRAVE_REWARDS_ENABLED)
  auto* rewards_service = RewardsServiceFactory::GetForProfile(profile);
  rewards_service->DoSomething();
#endif
```

What does the standard prefer?
choices: Keep the `#if` guards — buildflags are always clearer than runtime checks
Add a `CHECK(rewards_service)` inside the `#if` block to catch misconfiguration
Let the factory return null when disabled; callers just null-check
Move the guard into a macro like `IF_REWARDS(...)` for brevity
explain: Prefer internal feature guards: the factory/service returns null or no-ops when disabled. Scattered buildflags at call sites lead to missing deps and maintenance burden.

choices: Keep `std::make_shared` but supply a no-op deleter so it never frees the request
Use `std::unique_ptr` so ownership is exclusive
Keep `shared_ptr` — shared ownership is allowed when there's a strong reason
Take a `const network::ResourceRequest&` and use it directly
explain: Don't take ownership of memory you don't own; pass unowned resources by reference or raw pointer. `std::shared_ptr` is banned outright in Chromium — if shared ownership is truly unavoidable, use `scoped_refptr` with `base::RefCounted`, but prefer redesign.

prompt: A new code path calls into the ad-block service from a background task runner, and crash reports start appearing. What's the most relevant guideline?
choices: Service methods are thread-safe by default, so the crash must be coming from elsewhere
Check which thread the service method expects to be called on
Wrap the call in a `base::Lock` and it can then run on any thread
Switch to `base::ThreadPool` so the service runs on more threads
explain: Calling service methods from the wrong thread causes crashes. Always check the thread a method expects — especially for ad-block and shields services.

prompt: Which include should a reviewer accept in Rewards code that needs random utilities?
choices: `#include "brave/components/brave_rewards/core/engine/util/random_util.h"`
`#include "brave/vendor/brave_base/random.h"`
`#include "../../vendor/brave_base/random.h"` (relative path avoids visibility checks)
Either works as long as `gn check` passes
explain: Never `#include "brave/vendor/..."` to reach internal headers — they're not public API, and full paths shouldn't be used to bypass visibility. Use the component's public API header.

prompt: A PR adds a new `PrefObserver` interface with `OnPrefChanged(const std::string&)` so a class can react to `kMyPref` changing. What should the reviewer suggest?
choices: Poll the pref on a repeating timer instead
Use `pref_change_registrar_.Add(...)` (reusing the superclass's if it has one)
Keep the custom interface but derive it from `base::CheckedObserver` for safety
Observe the whole `PrefService` and filter by name in a switch
explain: Don't create custom observer interfaces for pref changes — use the existing `pref_change_registrar_` pattern. Also check whether the superclass already has a `pref_change_registrar_` before adding one.

choices: Drop the member and read the pref at call time; don't duplicate pref storage
Make `is_opted_in_` a `std::atomic<bool>` so reads are thread-safe
Also initialize `is_opted_in_` from the pref in the constructor so it's never stale
Keep it — caching prefs is a recommended performance optimization
explain: Don't duplicate pref storage. Caching a pref in a member just creates a second source of truth; read the pref when you need it.

prompt: `MyServiceFactory` builds a service that calls into `RewardsService` and `AdsService`. What must the factory constructor include?
choices: Nothing — keyed services are always created in alphabetical order
A `CHECK` in `BuildServiceInstanceFor` that the other two services already exist
A `PostTask` that delays creation until the other services are ready
`DependsOn(...)` calls for both factories' `GetInstance()`
explain: If your `KeyedServiceFactory` depends on other services, declare them with `DependsOn` so initialization (and shutdown) order is correct.

prompt: A service should never be active for incognito profiles. A teammate proposes overriding `GetBrowserContextToUse` to redirect incognito to the original profile. What's the preferred approach?
choices: Override `GetBrowserContextToUse` to redirect incognito to the original profile
Create the service anyway and early-return in each method when off-the-record
Return null from `GetForProfile` for incognito instead of redirecting
Put a `NOTREACHED()` in the service constructor for incognito profiles
explain: If a service shouldn't be active in incognito, the factory should give back null for that profile rather than overriding `GetBrowserContextToUse` to hand back another context.

prompt: A new component needs to download data files via the component updater. A teammate starts writing a `FooComponentManager` class. What's the standard?
choices: Write the manager — each component should have its own to isolate updates
Extend `BraveComponentUpdater` with a new subclass per component
Use a component installer policy — a per-component manager isn't needed
Download the files directly with a `SimpleURLLoader` instead
explain: Components don't need their own component manager — use a component installer policy instead.

prompt: Code in `components/omnibox` needs to ask the browser layer whether autocomplete is enabled, but including browser headers would be a layering violation. What's the recommended design?
choices: An abstract class in components, implemented in browser
Include the browser header but whitelist it in `DEPS` `specific_include_rules`
Use `g_browser_process` to fetch the client at runtime
Move the entire omnibox component into `brave/browser/`
explain: When components need browser-layer behavior, define an abstract base class in components and implement it in browser; components then use the abstract type without a layering violation.

choices: Nothing — returning the context unchanged is the correct default
It creates services for incognito; return `nullptr` if off-the-record
It should return `GetOriginalProfile()` so incognito shares the service
It must be marked `final` to prevent subclasses overriding it
explain: Never initialize services for profile types they shouldn't support (e.g. Rewards in incognito). `GetBrowserContextToUse` must return null for unsupported profile types.

prompt: A PR adds `brave_news::LocaleUtil`, a new singleton that determines the user's locale. `brave_ads::LocaleHelper` already exists. What should the reviewer say?
choices: Fine — each feature should own its own locale logic so teams aren't coupled
Make the new singleton a `KeyedService` instead
Copy `LocaleHelper` into `brave_news` so the two can evolve independently
Reuse the existing `LocaleHelper` rather than duplicating it
explain: Check for existing services and singletons before creating new ones — don't duplicate singletons for the same purpose. Prefer observers over adding direct cross-service calls for decoupled notifications.

choices: Add a `Cleanup()` method on the updater and call that
Add a shared free function `DeleteTorExecutable(path)` in a utils file
Keep it — each caller knows best when and how its files should be deleted
Post the `DeleteFile` to a background thread at each call site
explain: Cleanup logic belongs in the class that owns the resource. Don't spread cleanup details across multiple callers.

prompt: Where should a new Android-only Rewards native worker file go?
choices: `brave/browser/android/rewards/brave_rewards_native_worker.cc`
`brave/android/browser/rewards/native/brave_rewards_native_worker_android.cc`
`brave/browser/android/brave_rewards_native_worker.cc`
`brave/browser/brave_rewards/android/brave_rewards_native_worker.cc`
explain: Group files by component, not by platform: `brave_rewards/android/` beats `android/rewards/`. This keeps related code together, like Chromium's `chrome/browser/history/android/`.

choices: Keep it built and have each stub hit `NOTREACHED()` so misuse is caught at runtime
Wrap the whole target in `if (brave_wallet_enabled) { ... }`
Keep the declarations but delete the `.cc` from `sources`
Add a runtime `base::Feature` check inside each stub
explain: When a feature is disabled via buildflag, exclude the entire API from the build — don't leave API declarations with no (or empty) implementation.

prompt: A test needs to call `InternalMethod()`, which is private. A PR moves it to `public:`. What should the reviewer suggest?
choices: Make it `protected` and subclass the class inside the test file to reach it
Make it public but add a `// Visible for testing` comment
Keep it private and add a `friend` declaration for the test class
Duplicate the method's logic inside the test
explain: Use `friend` declarations instead of making methods public or protected for convenience. (`*ForTesting()` accessors are an accepted Chromium convention and aren't flagged under this rule.)

choices: Observers should be notified in reverse registration order
The lambda should capture a `WeakPtr` instead of `this` — otherwise it's fine as written
It should notify observers both before and after the query
Queries should return via a callback; observers are for state changes
explain: Callbacks for queries, observers for state changes. A Get/Fetch should return its result via a callback; observers fire only when something is Set, Created, or Deleted.

choices: The public Mojo type: `mojom::PublisherInfoPtr`
A forward declaration of `DatabasePublisherInfo` to avoid the include
A `void*`, so no internal header needs to be included
A `std::string` containing serialized JSON of the publisher info
explain: Never expose internal implementation types in public component headers; use the component's public API types (e.g. Mojo types).

prompt: In `brave/components/brave_referrals/BUILD.gn`, which target naming follows the standard?
choices: `source_set("referrals")`, referenced as `//brave/components/brave_referrals:referrals`
`source_set("brave_referrals_lib")` to make the target name globally unique
Name it after its directory, e.g. `source_set("browser")` in `browser/`
Any name, as long as it's listed in `visibility`
explain: GN `source_set` names should match their directory name, so paths are predictable (e.g. `//brave/components/brave_referrals/browser`).

prompt: The rewriter service is never null in production but is null in some unit-test configurations. Which snippet follows the standard?
choices: `if (!service) return;`
`if (!service) { CHECK_IS_TEST(); return; }`
`CHECK(service);`
`if (!service) { LOG(ERROR) << "null in tests"; return; }`
explain: Use `CHECK_IS_TEST()` before a null early-return when null should only happen in tests. It documents that null isn't a valid production state, unlike an ambiguous bare null check.

choices: Call the setter earlier, in `main()`, to avoid initialization-order issues
Store the callback in a global so any factory can set it
Pass the callback into the manager's constructor instead of a setter
Add a `DCHECK` that the callback was set before it's first used
explain: Pass dependencies via constructors, not setter callbacks. Constructor injection makes dependencies explicit and avoids confusing initialization ordering.

prompt: A `KeyedService` depends on local state that some unit tests don't provide, and the PR adds `if (!local_state_) return;` to several methods. What's cleaner?
choices: Keep the null checks and add a comment that they're only for tests
Override `ServiceIsNULLWhileTesting()` to return `true`
Create a fake local state in production so it's never null
Override `ServiceIsCreatedWithBrowserContext()` to return `false` in the factory
explain: When a keyed service shouldn't be created in unit tests lacking its dependencies, let the factory control it via `ServiceIsNULLWhileTesting()` returning `true` — cleaner than scattered null checks.

prompt:
Your service factory returns null for incognito, but a feature wants to work there too:

```cpp
auto* profile =
    Profile::FromBrowserContext(context)->GetOriginalProfile();
auto* service = MyServiceFactory::GetForProfile(profile);
```

What should the reviewer say?
choices: Don't bypass the factory; call it with the real profile and handle null
Good workaround — the original profile always has the service
Use `GetPrimaryOTRProfile()` instead of `GetOriginalProfile()`
Add a comment explaining why the bypass is needed, then it's fine to merge
explain: Never call `GetOriginalProfile()` (or similar) to circumvent factory profile checks. If the factory returns null for a profile type, that profile isn't supposed to use the service.

prompt: A helper must attach to the `WebContents` itself (it also runs on non-tab WebContents), but should be skipped for non-regular profiles and when `kFoo` is disabled. Which approach is recommended?
choices: Always call `CreateForWebContents()` and have every method check the guards
Make it a `BraveTabFeatures` member, even though it also runs on non-tab contents
Attach it unconditionally and destroy it in `DidFinishNavigation` if disabled
A static `MaybeCreateForWebContents()` with the guards
explain: For helpers that must live on the `WebContents`, use a static `MaybeCreateForWebContents` with the guards rather than always creating and checking internally. (Pure tab-scoped features go in `BraveTabFeatures` instead.)

prompt: You're adding a new keyed service factory for desktop. Which base class should it inherit from?
choices: `ProfileKeyedServiceFactory`
`BrowserContextKeyedServiceFactory`
`RefcountedBrowserContextKeyedServiceFactory`
`base::NoDestructor<KeyedServiceFactory>`
explain: New desktop keyed service factories should inherit from `ProfileKeyedServiceFactory` rather than the older `BrowserContextKeyedServiceFactory`.

prompt: Which change most clearly warrants a `base::Feature` guard?
choices: A one-line fix for an off-by-one bug in an existing, already-shipped feature
Renaming a private helper function
Fixing a typo in a log message
A large, experimental new service that may need rollback
explain: Guard significant or experimental functionality behind `base::Feature` so it can be remotely disabled via Griffin. Use judgment — small, self-contained changes and simple bug fixes typically don't need a flag.

prompt: A feature has `DesktopDelegate` (using `BrowserList`) and `AndroidDelegate` (using `TabModel`) with otherwise identical logic. What's the recommended refactor?
choices: Keep both delegates; platform code should always be fully separate
One unified delegate; only tab access is platform-specific
Merge them into one file with `#if BUILDFLAG(IS_ANDROID)` around every method
Move all the logic to Java and call it from desktop via JNI
explain: Unify platform-specific delegates: keep shared logic in one place and extract only the platform-specific bits (like tab access) into the delegate interface.

choices: It should use a `switch` statement instead of chained `if`s
`kImage` is a reasonable default since most uploaded files are images anyway
Unknown types silently become images; return `std::nullopt`
It should `CHECK` that `mime` is non-empty — otherwise fine
explain: Don't silently fall back on unknown types — silent fallbacks mask bugs. Return an explicit error (e.g. `std::nullopt`) and let the caller handle unknown types.

prompt: A Mojo `BookmarksListener` has a single `Changed(BookmarksChange)` event that fires both when the model finishes loading and when bookmarks actually change. Which design follows the standard?
choices: Keep `Changed` and add a `bool is_initial_load` field to the change struct
Separate `OnBookmarksReady()` and `OnBookmarksChanged()` events
Fire `Changed` on listener registration too so clients always get data
Remove the load signal; clients should poll until data appears
explain: A Mojo `Changed` event should fire only on actual data changes. Don't conflate lifecycle events (model load, listener registration) with mutations — provide separate events.

prompt: You need to fetch from three services in parallel and run `OnAllComplete` with all results. Which approach does the standard recommend?
choices: A `pending_count_` member that each callback decrements, running `OnAllComplete` at 0
Chain the fetches sequentially so the last callback has everything
`base::BarrierCallback<Result>(3, done)` passed to each fetch
A `base::RepeatingTimer` that polls until all results arrive
explain: Use `base::BarrierCallback` to aggregate parallel async results rather than manually tracking completion counts.

choices: Enum values must start at 1 in mojom
Mojom doesn't allow enums inside structs on any platform, so it won't compile
Nothing — nesting enums is preferred because it scopes the names
Nested enums break iOS codegen; move the enum to top level
explain: Mojom enums must be top-level when the target includes iOS; nested enums produce invalid Objective-C++ (`*.mojom.objc.mm` build failure).

prompt: `brave_wallet` must build for iOS. A PR adds a method taking `content::WebContents*` to a wallet service. What should the reviewer request?
choices: Pass specific deps like `PrefService*` instead of content types
Wrap the method in `#if !BUILDFLAG(IS_IOS)` and keep using `content::WebContents*`
Use `content::BrowserContext*` instead, which is available on iOS
Add `//content` to the iOS deps of `brave_wallet`
explain: Components that build for iOS can't depend on content-layer types (`content::WebContents`, `content::BrowserContext`) because iOS uses WebKit. Pass specific dependencies instead.

prompt: `brave_shields` must work on iOS and on content-based platforms. In the layered structure, which statement is correct?
choices: `core/` may depend on `content/` as long as the iOS build skips those files
iOS builds pull in both `core/` and `content/`
Put everything in `content/` and stub it out for iOS
Business logic lives in `core/`, which has no `//content` deps
explain: Use a layered component: `core/` is iOS-compatible with no `//content` deps and holds business logic; `content/` depends on `core/` and `//content`. iOS only builds `core/`.

prompt: Component A depends on component B. A new PR makes B call into a class in A. What's the recommended fix?
choices: Break the cycle with a delegate interface or observer
Allow it, since GN permits the cycle via `allow_circular_includes_from`
Merge A and B into a single component
Use a forward declaration so B doesn't need A's header
explain: Component dependencies must form a strict tree — no direct or transitive cycles. Use delegate interfaces or observers to break cycles.

prompt: A new Mojo data decoder service is being added. Where should its implementation live?
choices: In `components/<feature>/browser/` next to its callers
In a `services/` directory
In `components/<feature>/renderer/`
In `brave/browser/<feature>/`
explain: Mojo service implementations and data decoders belong in `services/`, not `components/.../browser/`, following Chromium conventions.

prompt:
```gn
# components/services/brave_shields/BUILD.gn
deps = [
  "//brave/components/brave_shields/core/browser/adblock",
]
```

What's wrong, and how is it fixed?
choices: Nothing; everything under `core/` is safe for all processes by definition
Use `public_deps` instead of `deps`
Utility code can't use browser code; move it to `common/`
Move the service itself into `core/browser/`
explain: Code running in the utility process must never depend on browser-process code. Anything shared between processes belongs in `common/`, not `browser/`.

prompt: A model-list service holds data that's identical for all profiles and doesn't depend on profile state. A PR adds a `BrowserContextKeyedServiceFactory` for it. What's the preferred design?
choices: Keep the KeyedService for consistency with the other services in the feature
A `base::NoDestructor` singleton, since there's no per-profile state
A global `ModelListService* g_model_list = new ModelListService;`
Store it as user data on each `BrowserContext`
explain: When a service has no per-profile state or profile-specific data, use a static singleton with `base::NoDestructor` — a KeyedService adds unnecessary complexity.

prompt: A migration you're writing would clear several user preferences and wipe a local storage directory on upgrade. What should happen before implementation?
choices: Flag the destructive operation for UX review
Ship it behind a feature flag defaulted on and skip review
Just log the deletion so it's debuggable later
Ensure it runs on a background thread so it's unnoticed
explain: Operations that delete user data must be flagged for UX review before implementation — silent data deletion is a poor experience and may violate user expectations.

prompt: You fire N parallel async requests and need results in the original request order. Which approach does the standard recommend?
choices: Insert into a `std::map<int, Result>` keyed by index, then copy it out at the end
`push_back` in each callback, then sort by timestamp
Pre-size a vector to N and assign each result at its request index
Issue the requests serially to preserve order
explain: For ordered async aggregation, pre-allocate a vector and insert by index rather than using a map and sorting later.

prompt: `mojom::ToolConfig` already has `name` and `description`. A PR adds a C++ `struct ToolConfig { std::string name; std::string description; };` plus conversion code. What should the reviewer say?
choices: Good — C++ business logic should never depend on generated mojom types
Fine, but put the struct in a `common/` directory
Add `static_assert`s to keep the two structs in sync
Use `mojom::ToolConfigPtr` directly
explain: When mojom types already describe the data shape, use them in C++ instead of creating redundant structs — duplicates create sync burden and drift risk.

prompt: Which API signature follows the standard for a fetcher with internal caching?
choices: `void FetchData(const std::string& url, Callback cb);`
`void FetchData(const std::string& url, const std::string& cache_key, Callback cb);`
`void FetchData(const std::string& url, int cache_slot, Callback cb);`
`std::string FetchData(const std::string& url, Callback cb);` returning the key
explain: Don't expose cache keys in API interfaces. Auto-generate unique keys internally instead of making callers provide or manage them.

prompt: The WebUI wants pinned items shown first, grouped by category. A PR changes the core service to return items in that display order. What's the better approach?
choices: Sort in the core layer so every client automatically gets the same UI ordering
Keep canonical order in the backend; reorder in the UI
Add a `display_order` field computed by the backend
Have the service return two lists: canonical and UI-ordered
explain: Data reordering for UI presentation belongs in the client/UI layer. The backend returns data in its canonical order; the frontend transforms it for display.

prompt: A history mojom interface will be consumed by WebUI and native iOS UI. Which name fits the standard?
choices: `interface HistoryPageHandler`
`interface HistoryWebUIHandler`
`interface HistoryUIHandler`
`interface HistoryWebPageBridge`
explain: Mojom interfaces that may be used by different UI frameworks should use framework-agnostic names like "UIHandler", not web-specific ones like "PageHandler".

prompt: A trusted WebUI page needs to exchange data with an untrusted `chrome-untrusted://` frame it embeds (which doesn't intentionally run untrusted code). What's the recommended channel?
choices: `window.postMessage` with origin checks
A shared `localStorage` key both frames poll
URL fragment changes on the iframe
A mojo interface between the frames
explain: Use a mojo interface for trusted/untrusted WebUI communication; Chromium advises against `postMessage` across trust boundaries. Only avoid mojo when the frame intentionally runs untrusted code and minimizing API surface is a deliberate security choice.

choices: Cache `kShieldedEnabled.Get()` in a function-local static to avoid repeated lookups
Drop the WebUI check here and gate it in the UI layer
Reorder the checks so the cheapest runs first
Also check `IsWalletWebUIEnabled()` in every caller
explain: Gate UI restrictions at the UI layer, not in core utility functions. Coupling core logic to UI state causes unexpected test failures and tight coupling.

prompt: An admin disables a feature via policy with ENFORCED enforcement. How should the settings UI behave?
choices: Show the controls greyed out with a managed icon
Show the controls enabled but ignore user changes
Hide the feature's UI section entirely
Show it normally — policy only affects the backend
explain: For ENFORCED policy-disabled features, hide the UI entirely rather than just disabling controls. RECOMMENDED policies keep the UI visible since users can override (and macOS `defaults write` creates RECOMMENDED policies).

prompt: A tester sets a policy with `defaults write` on macOS to disable a feature, and the settings section is still visible. Is that a bug?
choices: No — `defaults write` creates RECOMMENDED policies
Yes — any managed policy, regardless of level, must hide the UI
Yes — `defaults write` creates MANDATORY policies, so the section should be hidden
No — macOS never supports enterprise policies
explain: Only ENFORCED policies hide the UI entirely. RECOMMENDED policies keep it visible since the user can override, and on macOS `defaults write` produces RECOMMENDED, not MANDATORY, policies.

choices: Notify before assigning so observers can see the old-to-new transition
Post the notification asynchronously to batch updates
Fine — observers should handle redundant notifications themselves
Store the old value and notify observers only if the value changed
explain: Check that the value actually changed before firing state notifications to avoid unnecessary observer calls and re-renders.

prompt: A VPN feature needs a small helper that currently lives inside the Rewards module, and the PR imports the Rewards class directly. What's the recommended approach?
choices: Import it — reusing existing code is always better than any duplication
Copy the Rewards class into the VPN module
Make Rewards depend on VPN as well to keep things symmetric
Extract the helper into a shared utility or interface both can use
explain: Feature modules shouldn't import classes from unrelated feature modules. Extract shared functionality into a common utility or abstraction — cross-feature coupling makes features hard to change or remove independently.

prompt: Both Rewards and Wallet need the `gate3` service URL, with no single owner. Where should it live?
choices: In the `brave_domains:urls` target
As a `kGate3Url` constant duplicated in each component's `constants.h`
In the legacy `brave_constants.h`
In Rewards' constants, with Wallet adding a dependency on Rewards
explain: Shared URL constants with no clear owner go in `brave_domains:urls` — not duplicated per component and not in legacy `brave_constants.h`. Use `GetServicesDomain()` for environment-aware URLs.

choices: Keep it optional, since optional arrays are cheaper to serialize over IPC
Use `map<string, bool>?` instead
A non-optional `array<string>`; empty means no items
Add a separate `bool has_queries` field
explain: Prefer non-optional arrays in mojom (empty = no items). Only use `array<T>?` when null has a distinct meaning from empty.

prompt: A PR adds a new locale helper class under `brave/components/l10n/`. What's the reviewer's response?
choices: Fine — `components/l10n/` is where all Brave locale-related code is meant to go
It's deprecated; use Chromium's built-in localization
Fine, as long as it has unit tests
Move it to `components/l10n/common/` instead of `browser/`
explain: Don't add new code to the deprecated `components/l10n/`. Use Chromium's built-in localization; if no equivalent exists, discuss alternatives first.

prompt: A feature manages per-tab page-action state (e.g. find-in-page-like UI). Which owner is the right scope?
choices: `BrowserWindowFeatures`
A `BrowserContextKeyedServiceFactory` service
`GlobalFeatures`
`TabFeatures` (`BraveTabFeatures`)
explain: Every feature belongs to exactly one ownership primitive — Tab, Browser Window, Profile, or Global — and should use the narrowest scope that fits. Per-tab state belongs in `TabFeatures`.

prompt: A browser-window-scoped feature (e.g. a vertical tabs controller) wants to store a per-profile preference cache. What's the problem?
choices: Multiple windows can share a profile; keep profile state out
None; windows and profiles are always one-to-one
It should be moved to `GlobalFeatures` so every window and profile can share the cache
It should store the cache on each tab instead
explain: Browser-window features must not hold profile state (multiple windows share a profile), and tab features must not hold window state (tabs move between windows). Profile-scoped data belongs in a keyed service.

choices: Iterate by index (`for (size_t i = 0; i < size(); ++i)`) so growth is safe
Call `pending_callbacks_.clear()` before the loop
`std::exchange` the queue into a local, then iterate the local copy
Reserve extra capacity in `pending_callbacks_` before iterating
explain: Swap-and-process: move the queue into a local before iterating. Items added during processing won't corrupt the iteration or cause infinite loops.

choices: None; a tab's `Browser` never changes over its lifetime
Tabs can change windows; hold the `TabInterface` and ask it
Use `raw_ref<Browser>` instead of `raw_ptr` to prevent nulls
Store a `BrowserWindowInterface*` instead of `Browser*`, which is the modern API
explain: Tab-scoped features must never hold window-level objects (`Browser*` or `BrowserWindowInterface*`) — tabs can be dragged to other windows, causing use-after-free. Hold the tab and ask it for its current window.
